pairs.subject: image-to-3d-input-gating
pairs.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts:37 The gate asks the vision judge for free-text defects and a prose verdict sentence instead of a closed vocabulary and a closed verdict token, so defect classes cannot be counted across a batch and severity cannot be derived from class in the caller.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts:37 DEFECTS is open free text and VERDICT is a sentence, not a closed token. The three honest states (ran/unavailable/skipped) and enforcement at the paid route are realized, but the closed vocabulary is not, and the middle band generates (route.ts:130).

src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts:83 Isolation and in-frame are scored criteria (lines 30-33), but the frame-edge rule is not a hard fail regardless of score. The code's own arena admits cropped chest-up inputs at score 9.
src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts:32 The pose criterion is in the rubric. The limb-touching-torso and off-frontal hard-fail sub-rules fold into the single score rather than standing apart.

src/lib/visual-gen/reference-roles.ts:41 One 'style' role carries both lighting/colour and material, which the technique says must be split. The assembler (lines 173-182) also never rejects two identity masters or untagged duplicates, and it has no caller.
src/app/api/visual-gen/generate/route.ts:137 Only single-image mode is gated. multiview-to-3d submits go to the provider with no per-view gate and no set-consistency check.

pairs.registryProposal: score-defect-verdict-protocol gives one default band (pass >= 7, fail < 5), but input-gate.ts:79-87 measured that graders spend the 0-10 scale differently. A local 27B model scored clearly bad inputs 5-9, so its refit line is pass 9 / fail 8, which leaves a one-point middle band. The technique should say that thresholds are a (grader, line) pair refit per judge on a labelled truth set, and that the middle band's width is part of that per-judge fit.

pairs.subject: image-to-3d-input-gating
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/visual-gen/scene-composer/useSceneDressStore.ts:88 The scene-dress decomposition sends only the image and an opt-in crop-gate flag (default false, line 62), with no declared inventory from a brief. A missing object can never show up as residue, and an empty partition is reported as an honest 'empty' answer (line 96) rather than a loud failure.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/visual-gen/scene-composer/useSceneDressStore.ts:88 There is no expected-inventory declaration before decomposition, no coverage check and no residue state. Per-region crop gating exists but is opt-in.

pairs.subject: image-to-3d-input-gating
pairs.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/scene-crop.ts:7 Scene gating scores each extracted crop (step 3 of the technique) but never checks the partition itself against a declared inventory, so an object no box selected is absent with every per-crop verdict green.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/scene-crop.ts:7 Crops are scored on the extracted region, which is correct. There is no coverage check, no region/backdrop/residue three-state record, and no minimum-over-regions frame verdict.
src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts:208 Only 'fail' refuses spend. The middle-band 'warn' (line 105) proceeds to generation instead of prepare-and-re-gate.

src/lib/visual-gen/mesh-split.ts:12 mesh-split separates independently shipped props after generation. The technique excludes parts that ship independently, and no single subject is cut into parts here.
